# smtpfast_contact_property (Resource)

A declared custom contact field. Declaring is optional, since contacts can carry undeclared properties, but it gives the field a default for contacts that have no value and turns on type checking for writes to it.

Deleting the declaration leaves the values stored on contacts in place, so declaring the key again finds them.

Needs a provider API key with the `contact:read` and `contact:write` scopes.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Declared contact fields, with the defaults templates and broadcasts use when
# a contact has no value.
resource "smtpfast_contact_property" "plan" {
  key            = "plan"
  type           = "string"
  fallback_value = "free"
}

resource "smtpfast_contact_property" "seats" {
  key            = "seats"
  type           = "number"
  fallback_value = "1"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `key` (String) The property key, such as `plan`. 1 to 64 letters, digits, underscores, dots or hyphens. The built-in merge tags (`email`, `first_name`, `last_name`, `unsubscribe_url`, ...) cannot be declared. Changing this forces a new resource.
- `type` (String) `string` or `number`. Changing this forces a new resource.

### Optional

- `fallback_value` (String) Used when a contact has no value. Always written as a string; for a `number` property it must be a number, such as `"0"`. Up to 500 characters. Updates in place; omit it for no default.

### Read-Only

- `created_at` (String) Creation timestamp (RFC 3339).
- `id` (String) Unique identifier of the contact property.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import by contact property id.
terraform import smtpfast_contact_property.plan cp_abc123
```
